Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency/observability story. Legal at Medspring reviewed the DPA and sent back a redline (attached: redlined_DPA_v3.docx). A few high-level items they flagged that I wanted to surface:

- Processor/Controller role language: they want explicit confirmation of our ability to act as processor for model inference and a more explicit subcontractor (subprocessor) handoff clause.
- SCC applicability: they asked if we can sign the new EU SCCs and whether the DPA should reference them directly.
- KMS & key custody: procurement wants to confirm whether customer-managed keys are supported in a Private deployment.

Their target is to get DPA and order form agreed within two weeks so procurement can complete PO and DocuSign. Can we put together a short mutual action plan and owners? I attached the redline for context.

Proposed next step: 30–45 min sync tomorrow or Wednesday to triage legal asks and map owners. Do any of you prefer a specific cadence?

Thanks,
Emma

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and SCCs questions (attached)

Naomi / team — quick read of Emma's redline. A couple of practical positions to propose (short bullets):

1) SCCs: we can sign the current EU SCCs; recommend adding a line that the DPA incorporates the latest SCCs by reference and that we will use documented transfer impact analysis where required. That avoids re-drafting the full SCC text into the DPA.

2) Roles: Medspring's redline broadens "Controller/Processor" language. We should accept the processor confirmation for inference, but push back on any broad "controller-like" obligations (e.g., obligations to direct processing method). Offer to add a short appendix mapping responsibilities (controller = customer; processor = Redwood) — provides clarity without changing MSA liability framing.

3) Subprocessors: propose retaining our existing subprocessor notification flow (30-day notice + published subprocessors) and offer to include an initial list and a commitment to update prior to onboarding key cloud subprocessors. No need for contractual prior approval for every subprocessor — that will block operations.

4) KMS: customer-managed keys are available in Private deployments; for Hosted/Dedicated we can offer Bring-Your-Own-Key via KMS integration on a committed-case basis (requires a SOW and additional security review). Recommend flagging this in the order form as an optional add-on.

I can draft suggested redlines this afternoon. Please confirm if we want to surface the transfer impact addendum (TIA) as a separate deliverable or fold a short transfer statement into the DPA.

— Karthik
